notes: Three distinct datasheet failure modes for one symptom, plus a hard safety instruction (file the anode, never the cathode) that a partially-retrieved answer can invert.

turns.content: DO has gone erratic — jumping around instead of tracing a smooth curve.

must_contain: names zinc-oxide corrosion building up around the anode as a cause of irregular readings
gives the reconditioning steps: file the corrosion off the anode, not the cathode, then refill electrolyte and reassemble
names a worn membrane as another cause of irregular readings, remedied by replacing the membrane cap
must_not: invents a failure mode absent from the datasheet

turns.content: Could it just be that the water is still?

must_contain: states the galvanic probe consumes a small amount of the oxygen it reads, so some water movement is required
gives the figure of approximately 60 mL/min
concludes stagnant water can depress or destabilise readings
